title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 29-31): Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, collar-based theory of stratified spaces (the 'déploiement' of a stratified space into pieces glued along cylinders). The data are as follows. X is a space with a family (X_i)_{i in I} of closed parts ('closed strata'), indexed by a poset I. Each X_j carries a system of cylindrical neighbourhoods E_{j;·} ≅ B × [0,1]^J, i.e. compatible collars of the 'boundary' pieces B, as on a manifold with corners.

This page does three things.

(1) It finishes the definition of transversality between closed strata X_h ⊂ X_j for h ≤ j. One asks for a cylindrical neighbourhood of X_j and one of X_h inside X_h such that the inclusion X_h → X_j induces a morphism of cylinders, compatible with the cylindrical (product) structures. In addition one asks that the cylinder of X_h is the preimage under the projection p_{jh} of the cylinder of X_j (E_{h;h} = p_{jh}^{-1}(E_{j;j})). In modern terms the collars are required to restrict to collars and to commute with the projections. This is a collar-theoretic analogue of Mather's control conditions π_h π_j = π_h and ρ_j π_h = ρ_j.

(2) It defines a system of cylindrical neighbourhoods (of the X_j, inside the X_j) to be compatible with the stratification when, in condition b of p.29, the E_{j;j'} are mutually compatible for fixed j. The same is defined for germs of such neighbourhoods. A 'stratification cylindrique' is a stratification equipped with such a 'cylindrical structure', or equivalently with germs of cylindrical neighbourhoods. A NB asks whether a (pre)cylindrical stratification is 'equisingular'. This seems stronger, and he defers it to later.

(3) He notes a forgotten axiom, the one recorded as (14a) on the previous page: for all i, j in I, X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{h ≤ i,j} X_h. This is a strong frontier/intersection condition: intersections of closed strata are unions of closed strata indexed by common lower bounds. It implies X_i ⊂ X_j for i ≤ j.
- Corollary: if X_i ∩ X_j ≠ ∅, then i and j have a common minorant h with X_h ≠ ∅.
- The marginal NB records the trivial converse: a common lower bound h with X_h nonempty forces X_i ∩ X_j ⊃ X_h ≠ ∅.

The next page uses (14) to show that minimal strata X_β meet the other closed strata either trivially or by inclusion. This allows the inductive step: remove a conic neighbourhood of the minimal strata and recover the whole system from the complement plus boundary data.
errors: No genuine mathematical error. The corollary only yields a common lower bound h (with X_h nonempty), not a greatest one. The 'plus grand' in the transcription is not supported by the image and would be false in general (several maximal common minorants may exist).
Equisingularity of cylindrical stratifications is merely raised as a question, not established.

ideas.what: Transversality/compatibility of cylindrical neighbourhoods (collars) of nested closed strata: the inclusion induces a morphism of cylinders, and the smaller cylinder is the preimage under the projection of the larger one.
ideas.modern_name: Control data / commuting tubular-neighbourhood systems (Thom-Mather), in collar form; iterated fibration structures on manifolds with corners
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970/2012); collar form: Verona (1984), Albin-Leichtnam-Mazzeo-Piazza (2012), Ayala-Francis-Tanaka (2017)
ideas.where_published: Only alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 (dévissage of stratified structures in tame topology)

ideas.what: Definition of a 'stratification cylindrique': a stratification equipped with a compatible system (or germs) of cylindrical neighbourhoods.
ideas.modern_name: Thom-Mather abstract stratified set / conically smooth structure / system of compatible collars
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the programme only, not this definition

ideas.what: Axiom X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{h ≤ i,j} X_h for closed strata indexed by a poset, with the corollary on common minorants.
ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition / poset-stratification with closures meeting in unions of closures (stratification over a poset, intersection-closed)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Whitney, Thom, Mather; Lurie's poset-stratified spaces)

ideas.what: Question whether cylindrical stratifications are automatically equisingular.
ideas.modern_name: Topological local triviality along strata (Thom's first isotopy lemma consequence)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's collar-based 'cylindrical stratification' (cylinders on closed strata whose restrictions are preimages under projections) is essentially the structure later formalized as resolving a Thom-Mather/conically smooth stratified space into a manifold with corners carrying compatible collars (iterated fibration structures). It is an early, uncredited formulation of the 'déploiement' later done by ALMP and Ayala-Francis-Tanaka. On this page, however, only definitions appear.
missed.quote: l'application X_h → X_j induise un morphisme sur les cylindres (compatible avec les structures cylindriques) et de plus E_{h;h} = p_{jh}^{-1}(E_{j;j})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest: it documents Grothendieck's concrete approach to the 'théorème de dévissage' announced in the Esquisse. Mathematically it is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of routine definitions (compatibility of collars, the frontier-type intersection axiom, a trivial corollary). They match known Thom-Mather / manifold-with-corners notions. The only interest is historical: it documents Grothendieck's unpublished déploiement programme.
transcription_corrections: Corollary reads 'les i,j ont un minorant h (tel que X_h ≠ ∅ ...)'; 'plus grand' does not appear to be in the manuscript.
The cylinder equation is more plausibly 'E_{h;h} = p_{jh}^{-1}(E_{j;j})' than 'E_{h,j,h}'.

In the NB, 'est sûrement' appears struck out and 'cylindrique' is inserted above 'précylindrique'. The end reads roughly '"équisingulière" en semble plus fort que [X_i ∩ X_j ?] pourra introduire par la suite'.
Marginal NB likely reads: 'si i,j sont bornés inf. par h, alors X_i ∩ X_j ⊃ X_h ≠ ∅' (the converse of the corollary).
